blocks.heading: The shared block→HTML rendering engine every generator builds on — a typed `Block` vocabulary, per-type renderers and helpers, and an `assemble()` that turns a `Block[]` into one self-contained HTML document.

rows.value: `src` (the engine modules) + `src/renderers/*` (one renderer per block type).

Owns the `Block` union and the shared render primitives. `doc` feeds its `Block[]` straight to `assemble()`; recap, spec, and atlas ship their own shells that reuse core's renderers, markdown, and escaping.

bigIdea.label: The load-bearing idea
bigIdea.line: "One Block vocabulary and one set of render primitives — every product's page is built from the same core pieces."
bigIdea.sub: A product's job is to build blocks — diagrams, diffs, prose, file trees, annotated code. The plain-doc path is `assemble()`: it walks the `Block[]`, dispatches each block to its renderer by a `switch (b.type)`, inlines the CSS + viewer JS + dark-mode toggle assets, and returns one portable HTML string. The recap, spec, and atlas shells live in their own domains but build on the same union, renderers, markdown, and escaping — add a primitive once here and every generator can use it.

blocks.title: The pieces
blocks.intro: A typed block model at the center, one `assemble()` that walks it into an HTML shell, a fan-out of per-type renderers, and three helpers (highlight, lint, version). Tap a card to jump to its full section.

cards.name: block-model
cards.purpose: The `Block` discriminated union — the contract between products and the engine. Every renderable thing (diagram, schema, diff, prose, api, file-tree, annotated-code, questions, group, tabs, overview, example) is one variant, keyed by `type`.

cards.name: assemble + shell
cards.purpose: The pipeline: validate unique ids, render diagrams up front, dispatch each block to its renderer, then wrap the fragments in an HTML shell with inlined CSS + viewer JS + the dark-mode toggle (head-apply script, toggle button script, theme.css). `html.ts` supplies the escaping and safe-href guards the whole engine shares.

cards.name: renderers
cards.purpose: Ten renderer modules: eight pure `Block → HTML` functions (prose, diff, api, file-tree, annotated-code, questions, overview, example), plus the diagram color-key painter and the shared markdown substrate the prose/diff/overview renderers lean on. `assemble`'s `switch` calls the right one; groups and tabs recurse back through `assemble`.

cards.name: highlight
cards.purpose: Shiki-backed syntax highlighting behind a lazy singleton. `highlightCode` returns a full `<pre>`; `highlightLines` returns per-line inner HTML for the gutter-aligned diff and annotated-code grids. Both degrade to escaped plaintext on any failure.

cards.name: lint
cards.purpose: Non-blocking authoring guards. Walks the `Block[]` and warns — never throws — when a group lacks a description, a diff description is a wall of text, a diagram applies no color, an editable kind drops its mermaid, or there are too many / oversize diagrams. Also lints example blocks for mode/volume/contrast/synthetic issues.

cards.name: version
cards.purpose: The provenance stamp: `visual-skills@<git-sha>[-dirty] · <ISO timestamp>`, stamped into the page `<meta generator>` and footer. Falls back to the package.json version, then `"unknown"`, when git is unavailable.

blocks.title: How a document is assembled
blocks.intro: The `doc` product hands `assemble()` a `Block[]` (recap, spec, and atlas run their own shells on the same pieces). It validates ids, renders every diagram up front via the `diagrams` domain, then dispatches each block to its renderer and wraps the result in the HTML shell it builds — `escapeHtml` from `html.ts`, CSS + viewer JS + dark-mode toggle assets inlined. `highlight` and `lint` are helpers along the way; `version` stamps the page.

blocks.title: The pieces, in depth
blocks.intro: A full section per piece — what it does, how it works, its files and exports, and how it connects to the rest of the engine and the products that call it.

components.name: block-model
detail: `Block` is a discriminated union keyed on `type` — `diagram`, `schema`, `api`, `file-tree`, `diff`, `prose`, `annotated-code`, `questions`, `group`, `tabs`, `overview`, `example`. This is the entire contract between a product and the engine: a generator never touches HTML, it only constructs typed blocks. `assemble`'s exhaustive `switch (b.type)` is checked against this union, so adding a variant is a compile error until a renderer handles it.

Two variants are containers that nest **one level deep**: `group` (a labelled `<details>` of child blocks) and `tabs` (a CSS-only switcher, max 6 tabs). `diff` and `overview` may each carry an optional embedded `diagram`. The logic here is small and structural. **`childBlocks` / `withChildBlocks` are the single definition of the block tree** — the one list of places a block can hold another block (`group.blocks`, `tabs.tabs[].block`, `diff.diagram`, `overview.diagram`) plus its inverse. `walkBlocks(blocks, visit)` is the read-only depth-first traversal over that definition and `mapBlocks(blocks, fn)` its rebuilding twin (bottom-up, keeping container identity when nothing underneath changed). Every traversal in the codebase is built on those two — id assertions, diagram collection, the authoring lints, and normalization — so adding a container variant means editing one pair of functions. Hand-rolled `if (b.type === "group")` chains are what let tab- and diagram-slot-nested blocks be silently skipped. On top of the walker sit `isDiagramBlock` (the guard that finds every `diagram`/`schema` block for the up-front render) and the example normalizers: `normalizeExample` turns one hand-authored (possibly hostile) example into a safe block plus a list of problems and never throws; `normalizeExampleBlocks` is the assembler-boundary sweep every assembler runs over its incoming blocks **first** — `mapBlocks` reaches an example wherever it sits, replaces it with its normalized form and hands the problems back for the assembler to warn. It has to reach everywhere, because a nested example's raw `b.id`/`b.title` is read by `assemble`'s anchor step exactly like a top-level one's. `collectExamples` is the read-only counterpart the judgment lints use.

components.name: assemble + shell
detail: `assemble(blocks, opts)` is the plain-document pipeline — the `doc` generator calls it directly, while the recap/spec/atlas shells reuse its pieces rather than the function itself. It first normalizes every `example` block through `normalizeExampleBlocks` and emits that sweep's problems, asserts every block id is unique across the whole tree (anchors and in-page `#cross-links` depend on it), runs `lintBlocks` on the ORIGINAL blocks through `opts.onWarn`, then collects every diagram/schema block — nested ones included — and renders them up front. The id assertion and the diagram collector both run on `walkBlocks`, so they cover every container path by construction through the diagrams domain, keyed by id. It then maps each top-level block to HTML via `renderBlock`, a `switch (b.type)` that calls the matching renderer; `group` and `tabs` recurse. Finally it inlines `assets/template.css`, `assets/example.css` (the worked-example stage/rail/contrast styles), and `assets/viewer.js`, plus the dark-mode toggle assets — `assets/theme-head.js` (a synchronous `<head>` script that sets `data-theme` on `<html>` from `localStorage["vs-theme"]`/OS preference before paint), `assets/theme-toggle.js` (injects the `.vs-theme-toggle` button and wires click + OS-change), and `assets/theme.css` (appended after `template.css`/`example.css` in the `<style>`) — stamps an optional `<meta generator>` and footer, and returns a single self-contained HTML string — no external assets, by design.

`html.ts` is the tiny shared safety layer: `escapeHtml` (used by every renderer for any text that reaches HTML) and `SAFE_HREF`, the regex that allows only `#fragment` and `http(s)://` links so a `javascript:`/`data:` URL can't slip through the overview and review link renderers. `assemble` also injects each block's id as an anchor on its `<section>` so the cross-links resolve.

components.name: renderers
detail: Ten modules: eight per-block-type functions — `renderProse`, `renderDiff`, `renderApi`, `renderFileTree`, `renderAnnotatedCode`, `renderOverview`, `renderQuestions`, `renderExample` — plus `renderLegend` (the diagram color key) and the shared `renderMarkdown`. Each block renderer takes its block (some plus an `onWarn` or a pre-rendered extra) and returns an HTML fragment wrapped in a `vs-block` section; `assemble` adds the anchor and stitches them together. There is no shared base class — the union + the dispatch switch are the only structure. `renderExample` is the odd one out: it takes an `{ ownHeader, onWarn? }` opts object (not a bare `onWarn`) because its own-title-or-not choice differs by call site — a top-level doc section prints its own `<h2>`, while a recap section (top-level or nested in a walkthrough chapter) reuses the surrounding `section-header` instead. The same opts carry `preNormalized`, which every assembler sets: the block already went through `normalizeExampleBlocks` at the page boundary, which emitted its problems against the author's raw JSON, so the renderer's own (defensive, idempotent) re-normalize stays silent rather than duplicating and renumbering them.

`markdown.ts` is the substrate: `renderMarkdown` parses GitHub-flavored markdown, highlights fenced code via the highlight module, and runs the result through `sanitize-html` with a strict tag/attribute allowlist; `renderInlineMarkdown` does the one-line variant for headlines and bullets. `prose`, `diff`, and `overview` all build on it. `diff` and `annotated-code` use `highlightLines` to align highlighted code to a gutter; `file-tree` collapses single-child directory chains and links filenames back to their diff blocks; `legend` paints the auto-derived diagram color key.

components.name: highlight
detail: A thin wrapper over Shiki (dual `github-light`/`github-dark` themes with `defaultColor: "light"` — inline `color:` stays light-only, the dark palette rides along in `--shiki-dark`/`--shiki-dark-bg` custom properties that `theme.css` flips on for the dark-mode toggle — plus a fixed set of loaded languages) behind a lazy promise singleton, so the highlighter is created at most once per process. `highlightCode` returns a complete Shiki `<pre>` for fenced markdown code; `highlightLines` returns the inner HTML of each source line so `diff` and `annotated-code` can interleave code with gutters and per-line notes. `langFromPath` maps a file extension to a Shiki language id.

Every path is defensive: an unloaded language, a Shiki error, or a line-count mismatch degrades to escaped plaintext (and an `onWarn` note) rather than throwing — a highlighting failure must never break a document.

exports.desc: → per-line inner HTML (or `null`) for gutter-aligned grids.

components.name: lint
detail: `lintBlocks(blocks)` returns authoring warnings in document order — it never throws and never blocks rendering. `assemble` pipes them to `opts.onWarn`. The guards nudge quality: a `group` with no description, a `diff` description that is a long single paragraph (a wall of text), a `diagram` that applies no semantic color, an editable-eligible diagram kind that dropped its mermaid source (silently losing the Excalidraw upgrade), and too-many / oversize-edge diagrams overall. It walks the block tree with `walkBlocks` — the same traversal as its diagram collector, so group children, tab payloads and diagram slots are all covered — to collect every `example` block, and folds `lintExamples`'s findings into its own return, so `assemble` and `assembleReview` get example warnings for free just by calling `lintBlocks` — no separate call needed.

`lintExamples(examples)` inspects example blocks for quality nudges: checking for undersized step modes, long static walkthroughs (skipped when the *raw* block already asked for `mode: "step"` and normalization coerced it — that case gets the cap warning's "split it" instead), oversized stage bodies, dead reveals, unbalanced contrast sides, synthetic sources, and multiple reveal blocks on one page. Warnings only — normalization problems are surfaced once at the assembler boundary (`normalizeExampleBlocks`), not re-emitted here, so assemblers can call both without duplicates. Note it reads the blocks as the author wrote them, which is why every assembler lints `rawBlocks` and renders the normalized copy.
Both walk their respective block structures using judgment heuristics rather than hard constraints. The intent is to catch the mistakes that make a document read worse without making the build fail.

components.name: version
detail: `generatorStamp()` produces the provenance string `visual-skills@<git-short-sha>[-dirty] · <ISO timestamp>`. It shells out to git for the short SHA and a porcelain status (the `-dirty` suffix when the tree has uncommitted changes); if git is unavailable it falls back to the package.json version, then to `"unknown"`. The `recap` and `doc` CLIs pass the result as `opts.generator`, which the shell writes into the page `<meta generator>` and footer so any saved document records exactly which build produced it (the spec and atlas CLIs default to a static skill label instead).

blocks.title: Seams
blocks.intro: A small typed surface: products build blocks against the `Block` union and render through core's primitives; core in turn calls the diagrams domain to render every diagram up front.
blocks.note: [Authoring](../domain-authoring/domain-authoring.html)'s `doc` hands a `Block[]` to `assemble()`; [recap](../domain-recap/domain-recap.html), [atlas](../domain-atlas/domain-atlas.html), and the spec side of authoring ship their own shells that reuse core's `Block` union, renderers, and helpers. Core's only dependency is [diagrams](../domain-diagrams/domain-diagrams.html): `assemble` renders every diagram/schema block through it before dispatching the rest.
